trust_decision.summary: Whether an HTTP response body served with content-type application/vnd.hex+erlang by the configured Hex API server is deserialised as an Erlang term; at the pinned commit r3_hex_api:request/4 calls plain binary_to_term/1 on it (no [safe], no fun/port check).

landing_point.why: The advisory names 'unsafe deserialization of Erlang terms in hex_core'. The vendored tree has exactly one network-facing binary_to_term, and it sits in the hex API request function.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API r3_hex_api:get/post/put/delete (apps/rebar/src/vendored/r3_hex_api.erl:25-38), reached by the r3_hex_api_package/_release/_key/_user/_package_owner modules and by the CLI `rebar3 pkgs <name>` via apps/rebar/src/rebar_prv_packages.erl:52 -> apps/rebar/src/rebar_packages.erl:34
new helper r3_hex_safe_binary_to_term:safe_binary_to_term/1, called only from r3_hex_api:request/4

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No route outside the fix exists to dismiss. The only other binary_to_term calls read rebar's own _build cache files, and a solver could rightly say those are local, self-written state, not server responses.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate Hex API responses are maps and lists of binaries, numbers and existing atoms. A fix that rejects all atoms, or refuses to decode the erlang content type at all, breaks `rebar3 pkgs` and the publish/owner/key calls. A [safe]-only fix still lets funs through.

O6_input_shapes: fun nested inside a list, including an improper-list tail
fun as a map key or a map value
binary that creates new atoms (blocked by the [safe] option)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a repo-side endpoint (for example a mirror or legacy registry fallback) that decodes an erlang-typed body with binary_to_term instead of protobuf
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: r3_hex_api.erl:132 already notes that header code was copy-pasted from r3_hex_repo, so a duplicated response-decoding path in the repo client is plausible. It would be a WHERE-type sibling only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a rebar-side wrapper that caches the decoded API response to disk and reloads it with binary_to_term
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: rebar already persists package state with ets:tab2file/file2tab (apps/rebar/src/rebar_packages.erl:109). This would be a save/reload sibling, the only how-type option here.

O9_family: CWE-502 unsafe deserialization of untrusted Erlang external term format (funs and ports, plus atom-table exhaustion)

O10_build.toolchain: Erlang/OTP plus rebar3 bootstrap (./bootstrap); leex compiles r3_safe_erl_term.xrl at build time
O10_build.project_tests: None for r3_hex_api: apps/rebar/test has no references to hex_api, safe_binary or r3_hex_http. A pluggable http_adapter config (apps/rebar/src/vendored/r3_hex_http.erl:30) allows an offline test adapter.

j.j_sites_touched: apps/rebar/src/vendored/r3_hex_api.erl, apps/rebar/src/vendored/r3_hex_safe_binary_to_term.erl (new); other changed files are version-header bumps and a generated r3_safe_erl_term.erl
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change binary_to_term(RespBody) to binary_to_term(RespBody, [safe]). This stops new atoms but still accepts funs, so the recursive fun/port check gets skipped.

out_of_scope_notes: apps/rebar/src/rebar_compiler_dag.erl:52 and :406 and apps/rebar/src/rebar_erlc_compiler.erl:506 call binary_to_term on rebar's own _build cache files (local, self-written state).
apps/rebar/src/rebar_packages.erl:109 reloads the local package index with ets:file2tab (local cache, not a server response).
apps/rebar/src/rebar_utils.erl:809 file:consult on hex_metadata.config in a fetched dep dir (text terms; it cannot produce funs).
Package tarball metadata is already decoded with the safe lexer (apps/rebar/src/vendored/r3_hex_tarball.erl:431-434).
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check run)
the advisory's full text was not available; the trust decision rests on the fix diff and the summary only
